extracted.intended_audience: general readers and authors/researchers seeking information about Cleis Press (especially those interested in erotica, sexuality, LGBTQ, gender, and human-rights publishing)
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article describing the independent publisher Cleis Press: its founding, history, subject-area and genre focus, imprints, notable authors and titles, anthology series, and awards. Useful for authors researching fit or readers researching the press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject / genre focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Cleis Press is an American independent publisher of books in the areas of sexuality, erotica, feminism, gay and lesbian studies, gender studies, fiction, and human rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that fall within these topical areas (e.g., erotica, sexual education, feminist writing, LGBTQ studies, gender-related fiction/nonfiction, human-rights themed material) align with the press's mission. Examples of authors and titles published by Cleis Press are listed in the article (Susie Bright, Annie Sprinkle, The Whole Lesbian Sex Book, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication types: books, collections, anthologies, self-help guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication types: Books; Cleis Press produces many erotica collections and self-help sex guides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts both fiction and nonfiction book-length formats, themed collections/anthologies, and practical guides (sexual health/education). Representative titles include The Ultimate Guide to Fellatio and The Good Vibrations Guide to Sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erotica and sexual-content willingness
rubrics_metrics.description: Cleis Press produces many erotica collections and sexual-education/self-help titles and publishes erotic anthologies on diverse themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press publishes explicit erotic material across orientations and subgenres (e.g., Best Gay Asian Erotica, Best Lesbian Bondage Erotica, Best Erotic Romance series). They have ongoing/annual anthology series and curated erotic collections, indicating openness to erotic content and niche erotic themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Themed anthology / series publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of their collections include Best Gay Asian Erotica, Best Bisexual Women's Erotica, Best Lesbian Bondage Erotica, and annual anthologies titled Best Gay Erotica, Best Lesbian Erotica, and Best Women's Erotica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cleis runs recurring series and themed anthologies (including a yearly bondage erotica anthology starting in 2011). Submissions or works that fit a clear anthology theme or series are a match. Examples of editors and themed collections (Rachel Kramer Bussel, Alison Tyler, Kristina Wright, Mitzi Szereto) illustrate editorial curation by theme/genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-rights imprint focus (Midnight Editions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2000, Cleis Press founded Midnight Editions, a human rights imprint that aims to present fiction, nonfiction, and photojournalism from regions where repression and censorship are endangering creative expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Midnight Editions seeks work — fiction, nonfiction, and photojournalism — that documents or emerges from regions facing repression/censorship. Examples: The Little School by Alicia Partnoy; The Diary of a Political Idiot by Jasmina Tešanović.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transgender-issues and resources publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Cleis Press has also published a number of books on transgender issues, including Sex Changes: Transgender Politics and Body Alchemy: Transsexual Portraits. More recently they published The Transgender Child: A Handbook for Families and Professionals, a guidebook addressing social, legal, and medical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press publishes both personal/portrait-style works and practical guidebooks addressing social, legal, and medical topics related to transgender and gender-nonconforming people. Works that serve families, professionals, or document transgender experiences fit this axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissues / archival lesbian pulp fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction published by Cleis Press includes reissues of classic lesbian pulp fiction (including Ann Bannon's historic Beebo Brinker series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press is interested in reprinting historically significant or archival works within its topical remit (e.g., lesbian pulp fiction), indicating openness to restoration/resurrection projects and literary history editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of editorial recognition and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The press has been the recipient of many awards, including the Firecracker Alternative Book Award for Outstanding Independent Press twice (in 1997 and 1999), and several Lambda Literary Awards in 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past awards signal the press's reputation and editorial standards. While not a submission criterion stated on the page, award history indicates the press's engagement with quality work in relevant fields.
